title: Introduce cluster-aware latency echoes and traffic-anchored regression quarantine
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Existing canary detectors rely on aggregated latency/throughput signals that often miss short-lived, cluster-local regressions caused by scheduling, NUMA pressure, or kernel-level stalls. This PR introduces a lightweight, cluster-aware 'latency echoes' signal and a traffic-anchored quarantine policy that isolates suspect model-serving replicas for targeted evaluation before global rollout. Design summary: 1) Latency echoes: compute per-cluster micro-fingerprints by replaying a tiny subset of recent live requests as 'echo probes' to the same replica group. Echo probes run at low priority and measure tail latency amplification, kv-cache miss amplification, and context-serialization stalls. 2) Traffic anchoring: map live traffic cohorts (by route, prompt-size, and customer tier) to cluster affinity so quarantine decisions are scoped to the affected cohort rather than the whole fleet. 3) Temporal decay calibration: use an exponential decay window for echo aggregation so transient noise is downweighted while preserving sensitivity to persistent degradations. 4) Quarantine flow: when an echo fingerprint crosses configured thresholds, affected replicas are automatically moved into a quarantine ring (read-only shadow mode) and fed into an accelerated local regression evaluation that combines synthetic micro-probes and seeded shadow traffic. If regression is confirmed, rollout is halted and a rollback is triggered; otherwise replicas are reintroduced. Implementation notes: added an EchoScheduler, ClusterAffinity mapper, and a QuarantineOrchestrator. All components are feature-gated behind perf.canary.latency_echoes and can be toggled per-deployment. Backwards compatibility: detectors default to off and require the existing canary controller to be upgraded to v1.45+ for the quarantine step to work. Testing and validation: unit tests for fingerprint generation and decay math, integration tests that simulate node-local stalls, and a shadow experiment that ran for 48h on canary traffic with zero false positives at the tuned thresholds. Migration and rollout: rollout starts disabled, then enabled in a host-by-host canary on Dedicated clusters; ops runbook included. Related work items: ENG-8792 (design), ENG-8803 (ops runbook), SUP-1421 (customer incident that motivated local-quarantine behavior).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice isolation model. A couple of questions: how do we avoid amplification when multiple clusters echo concurrently? Suggest adding cross-cluster dampening.
Maya Chen: Reply to Arjun: we add a cross-cluster dampening coefficient and include it in the decay math; default is 0.6, configurable via feature gate. Added explanation in fingerprint.py docstring.
Lena O'Neil: Can we ensure quarantine doesn't affect billing or rate limits for customers? We should ensure shadow read-only mode is not counted against quotas.

Maya Chen: Reply to Lena: confirmed. Quarantine shadow traffic is tagged and excluded from billing and quota enforcement in the request-metadata layer; added tests and a migration note in the runbook.
Diego Ramos: Please add an observability dashboard for per-cluster echoes and a debug endpoint to dump fingerprints for troubleshooting.
Maya Chen: Reply to Diego: added grafana dashboard JSON and a /debug/echo-fingerprint endpoint behind an admin flag.
release_notes: Add cluster-aware latency 'echoes' and traffic-anchored quarantine: opt-in feature behind perf.canary.latency_echoes. Provides localized detection and isolation for node/cluster-local regressions; includes runbook and observability. Disabled by default; recommended gradual enablement for Dedicated clusters.
